checks.details: Exact intake and all 1677 source-file hashes match before/after; 33 overlays, 39 package files, 11 retained native artifacts and oracle artifact record verified. Package source inventory equals the test runner inventory. No extra source files.

HMAC-SHA256 has a fixed domain prefix, strict canonical request shape, fresh 32-byte challenges, case/invocation/preparation/anchor binding, request-hash and ordered response MAC binding. Endpoint verifies provisioned code, boot and complete namespace/device anchor. Controller matches provisioned daemon/code/host exclusions, never inferring expected host values from actor receipts. Replayed/modified/wrong-key/foreign-boot/namespace and delayed exchanges reject in 7 additional deterministic negative controls.

Owned-file probes reject wrong owner, group-readable key, symlink and multiple links. Actual service credentials/parent-directory protection/key distribution remain operator provisioning obligations. No actual configuration or secrets were read.

Control-byte handling checks the Linux deadline after a successful read before returning A/G/R. Conservative controller elapsed-time lease is not equated to Linux epoch. Existing boundary/high-uptime/expiry/dispatch tests pass. No native instruction executed; scheduling/runtime timing remains unproven.

checks.details: Exact retained target manifest regenerated in memory; AArch64 static PIEs have no writable-executable LOAD or executable stack. Actual embedded observer BPF equals retained/generated bytes; all 3 profiles match. Source bundle hashes match inventory and oracle record. Admission binds exact ELF/source/profile to case/scope, own metadata generation, namespace exclusions and target peer. Restart/namespace/ELF mismatch tests reject. Interpreter ELF was not supplied; its recorded hash and pinned image recipe are not runtime attestation.

96 mmap role/protection/flag combinations plus executable mprotect and setter denials checked. Oracle extra rule permits no PROT_WRITE and no MAP_ANONYMOUS bit; W+X and executable mprotect reject. 1000 ptrace request/TID/regset combinations from retained BPF, foreign architecture and post-admission exec reject as expected. No filter installed. Argument rules alone cannot attest actual FD provenance or effective mount noexec behavior; real OCI validation remains required. Shared target-written volumes are explicitly configured noexec/nodev/nosuid.

Shared volume noexec policy

checks.details: Canonical byte equality, duplicate/float/NaN rejection, 1024-byte frames, partial-EOF refusal and shared 65536-byte/64-frame budget verified. Context responses capped at 4096 bytes; kernel/file inputs bounded; witness is fixed 8480 bytes and client fixed 1024 C bytes. Adversarial untrusted fields are not reflected into stable error diagnostics.

Existing real-Python-pipe tests cover early/partial/stderr/EOF outputs, authorizer latency, target/observer admission expiries, no-oracle G refusal, matching-oracle R prerequisite, source mismatch and own-process transport cleanup. No Docker inspection is introduced on HELD/resume path. Point-in-time quiet checks are not future liveness guarantees.

checks.details: Witness no-follow/nonblocking regular/single-link/inode/owner/mode/size checks and two stable reads reviewed. Actual owned-file mode change between reads and final fstat rejects; UID/GID 999 observation was simulated, not privilege-changed. Socket code fixes pathname, validates pre/post inode/owner/mode and Linux peer UID/GID; data is bounded read-only. Existing real socketpair test preserves fragments, full completion and EOF. Actual Linux SO_PEERCRED/cross-private-namespace pathname admission was not executed.

checks.details: Stable original-generation remote stop checks correctly remain separate from socket/CLI EOF; existing restart and receipt-mutation controls pass. However closure client history is not checked: SEC-CTX-001 reproduces erased completion/error and fabricated cut credit. No actual remote stop or retirement is claimed by these fixtures.

checks.scope: Byte-preserving union of 39 package files and 33 overlay paths: 46 files only. No unrelated-work scans.

attack_preconditions: An actor or transport can supply oracle response bytes, as explicitly assumed by this review.
The owned oracle stream has passed admission; the attacker keeps the expected case, invocation, witness digest, sequence and predecessor hashes.
The separate original-generation target/oracle stop checks may all be genuine; the attack does not bypass them or require the context HMAC key.

cvss_3_1.scope: Qualitative local actor/transport control assumed by the review threat model; impact is oracle-evidence integrity, not a demonstrated host compromise.

evidence.description: Validates each summary in isolation; no monotonic history or proof that a HELD cut actually preceded CLOSE.
Case/sequence/chain validation does not constrain cross-phase client-state transitions or derive cut claims from a previously accepted HELD reply.
The bridge stores the receipt hash/sequence but not the previous client transcript; a correctly chained contradictory reply is accepted.
CLOSE is legal directly from INITIALIZED and its summary is retained without joining to accepted cut/client history.
closed_no_reply_window is derived solely from the final untrusted client summary after genuine stop-generation checks.

findings.impact: A single invocation can receive closed_no_reply_window=true despite an earlier accepted 1024-byte complete reply, an earlier transport error, or no accepted HELD cut at all. These false classifications undermine the bounded independent oracle. The objects still carry execution_authorized=false/runtime_evidence=false: this is not a claim of accepted native execution or M4 exploitation.

minimal_remediation.private_validation: Proposed helper rejected all 3 malicious recorded sequences and accepted 8 honest sequences, including no-cut close, non-stream, late complete reply, partial clean EOF, reset, unresolved close, acknowledged and unordered receipt.
required_regressions: Run the real bridge against each malicious responder variant and require fail-closed rejection.
Keep complete/error/cut state sticky across HELD, FINAL and CLOSE; test forged cut without HELD.
Retain positive late-complete, partial-EOF, reset, unresolved and non-stream controls.
retain_existing_controls: Own-stream binding, predecessor/sequence validation, witness identity
Original-generation remote stop inspections, clean client EOF, and all preparation-only flags
minimal_remediation.summary: Enforce controller-side client history, not just worker-side generation. Bytes must never decrease; an established completion timestamp and terminal error/EOF must not disappear; classification/cut must be immutable after HELD. Only a successfully joined HELD reply may introduce a cut. Derive late-completion from the retained cut bounds and require matched HELD history for no-reply credit.

reproduction.method: The real OracleSession, protocol validators and ProcessStream communicate with a benign owned Python responder over actual pipes. Bounded Docker/kernel admission and stable original-generation stopped metadata are synthetic fixtures; no Docker or native actor runs.

findings.title: Oracle closure trusts the last client summary, allowing erased replies/errors and fabricated pre-ACK cuts

limits_and_non_findings: No Docker operation, native actor/real sandboxed oracle execution, tracing/ptrace, kernel policy change, namespace join, real Redis case or deployment occurred.
Private Python fixtures and injected Docker/kernel data demonstrate validator behavior only, not Linux or Docker runtime feasibility.
Host source provisioning/secure parent directories/key distribution/Mac-to-Linux bounded transport remain explicit operator trust obligations; not recast as current code vulnerabilities.

The backend retains the legacy direct trusted-context dictionary path (docker_backend.py:352-358 and 437-440). The authenticated acquisition path enforces its anchor/key; the direct path still relies on an independently trusted outer caller, as runtime_admission.py:96-98 documents. No code was found automatically deriving expected host values from actor receipts. Runtime integration must not route actor-supplied dictionaries into this trusted-parameter API.
Point-in-time observations do not atomically guarantee future process lifetime, untouched memory, inode non-reuse or whole-trial confinement.

The original prior implementation handoff bytes were not supplied at an authorized path; its stated SHA256 is bound by the verified intake, not independently rehashed. All supplied intake/snapshot/inventory/native/oracle bytes were verified before and after.

The pinned Python base/interpreter identity record was checked, but no oracle interpreter ELF or full runtime image was available for independent library/OS/CVE inspection. No artifact-only build was rerun.

Prepare, review and admit exact target/observer/oracle runtime images, effective filters/mounts, interpreter/libraries, resources and actual cross-namespace socket behavior.
Complete trial dispatch, per-trial timing/evidence assembly, whole-trial confinement/resource monitoring and independent watchdog cleanup/absence joins.
Obtain separate exact-artifact and native calibration/execution decisions. Full M4 remains open.
